title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 46
summary: Personally inspect 40 roots: add 32 projects and record three duplicate/lineage consolidations and five deferrals.
notes: Root personally ran 48 wide searches yielding 322 hits and 322 distinct URLs, inspected 40 roots and prepared 32 additions with eight non-promotions: three duplicate/lineage consolidations and five deferred leads or architecture audits. Coverage includes original-source archives, ports/reimplementations, assembly/C reconstruction, translations, chip emulation, binary tools, developer workflows and hardware recovery across classic computers and consoles. Broad search does not establish every platform exhausted. No discovery worker used; no upstream software, game, emulator, ROM, firmware or installer executed. Current catalogues were refreshed at 30c8fe4200189b0f6e986056df6220dc8341ffa9; local activity history is older cached data, so live trusted-main validation remains required. Ingestion findings: stable repository IDs catch two renamed reconstructions missed by URL screening; alternate historical forks need lineage review rather than duplicate entries. A product name or README goal can conceal empty files or a placeholder UI. Native port, full-ROM matching, function matches, linked C bytes, naming percentages and lexical clean-source ratios are different measures. .c files can contain asm bodies; near-match C can be excluded from the build; vendor library source must not count as recovered game logic. The 3DO Company is not the 3DO console, and Android-through-Windows-compatibility is not a native Android build. Preserve explicit game-specific-emulation audit exclusions, region/toolchain prerequisites, known unfinished boss functions and audio simplifications. Hardware-chip conformance to a pinned reference is bounded evidence, not blanket analog/device correctness. Single-device NAND recovery does not generalize across units. Large recursive-tree failure was recovered via commit-pinned directory/file reads rather than silently treating the repository as empty. Historical generated scaffolding is distinct from semantically adopted source; byte exactness remains a build property rather than a single completeness percentage.

sources.reason: Scripts bridge Linux/WSL builds to host Windows WinAPE, loading disk images and NOI symbols on changes. Not a new CPC emulator or game engine.
New game code recovers original BASIC rules and formulas while replacing wording/art. Seeded Python RNG and formula tests do not prove identical original random sequences.
Partial initialization recovery with STRONG.DAT extraction/reassembly tooling and Borland overlay normalization. Palette/RLE and most game-code recovery remain unfinished.

C17/SDL3 engine recovers game rules and raw record widths; widescreen expands visibility checks and modern options intentionally change presentation. OPL/speaker emulation is an audio component, not a generic guest CPU game wrapper.
Banked assembly and memory/script maps from DiztinGUIsh. Code converted to assembly is not fully understood: README marks large semantic gaps and explicitly excludes audio disassembly.
Partial disassembly and edited assets support multiple translations. English completion does not imply all language variants complete; current source defaults select Latin Spanish and enable debug.
Source port includes enemy/gameplay logic and banked assets, but README records stage/boss routines removed to make a build succeed. Not a confirmed complete playable game.

Sequencer-level PSG core with variant data and clocked write behaviour. Upstream compares attenuation streams with pinned Nuked-PSG, but this is not blanket electrical or analog audio equivalence for every chip.
Print-routine analysis, extraction tools and SQLite script workflow support game1 translation. Repository title includes1&2, but game2 notes are future work.
Translation texts, character encoding notes and C text-formatting tool accompany the patch. Hardware/full-playthrough success is reported upstream, not independently verified here.
Graphics extraction/reinsertion uses ASCII-art representations to preserve palettes, with separate shop text patches and test saves. Translation largely concerns visual text, not only strings.
First pass covers functions but names, raw pointers and RAM semantics still need improvement. Matching output is the restoration gate, not a claim of complete understanding.
Partial USA disassembly includes typed compression-state names and documented mixed raw/RLE/reference encoding. Base ROM still required; generated matching output is not all source recovery.
Banked assembly, graphics tables and hardware/memory definitions exist despite minimal README. Many address-derived names remain; no completion percentage inferred.
16-in-1 menu source covers headers, interrupts, graphics and bank/menu handling. Scope is cartridge menu, not the games contained on a multicart.
Translation pipeline includes font/script resources, ROM preparation and insertion tools. A patched game is not an original byte-identical reconstruction.
Small focused patch replaces the single Japanese options screen with custom drawing code and compressed art. Rest of UI already English; do not inflate into whole-game text recovery.
Configurable splitter integrates spimdisasm/Rabbitizer and emits rebuild inputs. Symbols, section boundaries and analysis options require evidence; it is not automatic high-level C recovery.
Matching original-target reconstruction with region-specific code/data progress and recovered scheduler/audio structures. Not a PC port; original asset extraction remains required.
Source tree mixes recovered game code, included assembly stubs and original-library source. Library volume alone must not count as recovered game logic.
Source explicitly remains non-shiftable and contains many GLOBAL_ASM stubs beside C functions. Byte-matching target is not readiness for arbitrary modifications.
Guide includes a substantive script generating Ghidra function-ID databases from user SDK libraries. Goes beyond a link list, but is not a game decompilation or shipped SDK database.

CORE.GT4 engine matching is separate from Adhoc game scripts. README distinguishes matched functions, linked C/code bytes, tiny reconstructed-data fraction and a lexical clean-source metric; full build retains original assembly for gaps.
PAL2.00 reconstruction links recovered functions at original addresses and fills gaps from local disassembly. Readability refinement and future PC reimplementation remain separate work.

Stripped boot executable and overlays have recovered functions and layout metadata. Inspected near-match C is explicitly excluded from matching build and replaced by assembly; readable research code is not automatically linked code.

USA ADGE reconstruction reports auto-matched raw output and donor-reused functions separately. Inspected .c donor files contain asm bodies, so C extension and matched-count metrics do not establish idiomatic C recovery.
WIP uses donor symbols and animation C matching. README percentages count named symbols, not compiled-C completion; most code remains generated assembly.
Historical game source, editor tools and some artwork are archived together. The3DOCompany is publisher, not the3DO console target; original copyright notices remain.
CVBasic/assembly port preserves the source game loop while adapting audio, banking and input. Custom emulator supplies estimated timing, not independent hardware cycle proof.
Original-style line-numbered dungeon/inn/training BASIC and level files, including1979copyright/revision header. No README does not mean absent source.
Single-unit repair documents boot/NAND/FTL findings and includes bounded read-only digest tools. Working cold boot does not establish every NAND cell healthy or all historical data recovered.
Two-pass assembler supports labels/directives and emits address/code JSON for a separate emulator. The .6809 extension is text JSON, not a standard executable or raw ROM.

Inspected tree has empty game and engine files, a small script interpreter and a tiny assembly handler. No working Amiga game/engine implementation established; retain as a lead rather than promote the advertised game.

Repository title promises all Mega Drive games but README narrows to incomplete Game Genie work; tree contains README and GameGenie.bin only. No inspectable source or disassembly established at this revision.
Already tracked as solomons-key-nes-reconstruction under oranguthang. Old API redirects to repository ID1352704779, identical to the selected root; preserve owner-rename lineage.
Already tracked as castle-excellent-nes-source-reconstruction under oranguthang. Old API redirects to repository ID1352704427, identical to the selected root; do not duplicate for owner rename.

Retain for architecture audit, not promotion in this pass: playable component is explicitly EarthBound-only SNES emulation, while native Nim reimplementation is future work. There is genuine region-level assembly reconstruction, which must be separated from game-specific emulation before inclusion under the existing scope rule.

Architecture-audit backlog: game-specific ARM static recompilation plus DS hardware runtime, not recovered high-level game source. Current claim reaches opening credits/START only; no finished native port. Keep separate from ordinary matching decompilation and do not promote before scope review.

Current v2 source is a SwiftUI shell: openGame/export are placeholders and InspectorView renders placeholder text. README describes intended resource browsing, but implemented SCUMM decoding was not established in this tree. Retain for follow-up rather than advertise goals as delivered features.

Alternate copy/continuation of already tracked F9DASM: source credits Arto Salmi, Hermann Seib and Rainer Buchty and lists historical output/label fixes. No sufficiently distinct project scope established to warrant another entry beside Arakula/f9dasm. This is lineage consolidation, not a claim that GitHub IDs or revisions are identical.
